note: v27: item-forecast rollouts keep their policy when jokers are only removed (Madness, Ceremonial Dagger, Popcorn or Gros Michel running out): the removed jokers' entries are dropped instead of rebuilding the policy from the jokers' current text. Rust does the same, so Rust gives up on 1% of item rollouts instead of 19%. A small behaviour change in rollouts only: lab E+F on 28 seeds, 1 game of 28 changed per arm (-0.11 +- 0.11 ante, noise). 56/56 identical to JEV_NATIVE=0; 683 s -> 60 s. Based on: v26: speed only, same decisions as v25 on the new sim baseline. Item rollouts run in Rust from their first shop, including the bot's tarot/spectral use (use_items and tarots.plan ported, with the tarot table and build suit passed in). Rust gives up only when the jokers change. The Fool's last_tarot_planet is passed. The joker forecast's per-seed path now carries RNG streams and compares RNG state, not pickled bytes. Sim fixes (new sim baseline, real-replay parity still 329/336): a debuffed joker loses its passive (Stuntman hand size); SMODS fills grown hand slots at once; rumbot's Crimson Heart follows SMODS. Lab E+F on 28 seeds: 56/56 identical to JEV_NATIVE=0, 677 s -> 70 s. Based on: v25: speed only, same decisions as v24. The pack/tarot/spectral forecast's rollouts (rollout_items) hand off to rumbot-sim at the first shop holding no consumables, with Jackdaw's pseudoseed streams carried over (sim_bridge.run_strict, jev_sim.rollout_strict). Rust gives up (and Python carries on) when the bot would use a tarot or the jokers change at a blind select (Madness, Riff-raff, Popcorn): about 11% of handoffs. Lab arms E+F on 28 seeds: 56/56 identical to JEV_NATIVE=0, 670 s -> 83 s (8.1x). Sim also fixed: Smeared Joker applies to every suit check. Based on: v24 draft: speed only, same decisions as v23, in two parts. (1) jokers.score over every play subset (hands.evaluated_plays, best_score, best_play: odds forecasts, readiness, setup plays) and rollout.Policy's candidates run in a Rust kernel (native/, src/native.py); joker rules are data tuples instead of lambdas so both evaluate the same rule; every subset score identical (tests/test_native.py). (2) The shop forecast's rollouts (rollout.forecast) run on rumbot-sim in Rust (native/sim, src/sim_bridge.py): each option's Jackdaw state is converted once and rollout.Policy/play_horizon run in Rust, rows identical to the Python loop (150/150 jokers, 10,764 rollouts; 123/123 forecast options). Python stays the fallback (JEV_NATIVE=0 or modules not built). Pack/tarot forecasts (rollout_items) stay in Python. Based on: v23: early joker slots are filled by code. Through ante 3 with fewer than 4 jokers, when no shop option clears the 2 SE bar, code buys the joker the forecast rates best above buying nothing (any positive margin). On the 4 seeds where JEV v20 beat the code-only bot most (XYK41G5M, 68RZS4XR, R8ZXJN6L, 54ATPSF9), the code-only bot reached ante 2 with 0-2 jokers and died, while JEV filled slots and went to ante 6-9. Based on: v22: speed only, same decisions as v21 (per-seed results of the lab's arms E and F identical on 28 seeds): rollout copies by unpickling one snapshot instead of deepcopy; cash-outs inside forecast rollouts skip shop population; hands.classify memoised; tarots.auto_use builds the build plan only when a targeted card needs it. Based on: v21 draft: the policy lab's arm F in production (+0.44 +- 0.12 ante over v20's code path, 303 paired seeds). Packs, shop tarots and shop spectrals get their own rollout forecast (rollout_items.py: packs opened with sampled contents and the Picker rule, tarots used on tarots.plan targets) in what is left of the 4 s shop budget; one that beats buying nothing by > 2 SE is bought by code after any joker auto-buy, and JEV sees the same forecast fields on every pack/tarot/spectral. In an open pack the Picker's card is taken by code when its value is >= 1.25x the runner-up's, otherwise JEV rates the cards with a pick_value field. Forecast exceptions are logged with tracebacks to runs/_forecast_errors.log; fixed a KeyError in the forecast state when Fortune Teller is owned. Based on: v20 draft: the policy lab's arm C in production. Forecast horizon 3 bosses (n=24); a forecast option that beats buying nothing by > 2 SE in blinds cleared is bought by code (recorded as an 'auto' shop event with its numbers), without a JEV question; JEV still rates close calls, packs, tarots, spectrals and economy items with the forecast fields (survive_2_bosses and blinds_cleared_next_6 renamed survive_horizon and blinds_cleared_horizon); reroll rule kept; rollout guard for an empty deck and hand. Based on: v19 draft: rollout forecast in the shop (rollout.py). Each joker, planet, voucher and swap is simulated through the next 2 bosses with the build frozen (32 rollouts, common random numbers); JEV sees next_boss_clear vs skip (paired difference and SE), survive_2_bosses, boss_margin and blinds_cleared_next_6 instead of measured_gain/readiness_after. Code: sure buy at > 2 SE over skip, hide items > 2 SE worse (unless economic), reroll when nothing beats skip by 1 SE, swaps only sell the 2 weakest jokers; v18 path when the forecast fails. Packs/tarots unchanged.
rules: Balatro: reach each blind's chip target before hands run out. A hand scores chips x mult; jokers add chips or mult, or multiply mult (xMult). Discards are free but limited. Interest: $1 per $5 held at round end, max $5 (at $25).

instructions.blind: Should we play or skip the upcoming blind?
instructions.play_now: Should we play our strongest hand (`strongest_play`) now instead of discarding first to build a better one? `best_draw_by_measurement` compares the best draw plan with playing now: its average includes misses, and poor_draw_next_play shows downside. Weigh the measured improvement and chance of meeting pace against spending one of our remaining discards. Preserve discards when we are on pace and the improvement is small. Survival this round comes before build preference.
instructions.best_play: Which play is best this turn? `estimated_score` already includes our jokers (except any in `jokers_not_in_estimates`), but are approximate. Prefer the higher score unless a lower one keeps stronger cards or avoids resetting a scaling joker.
instructions.setup_play: When `next_hand_outlook` is present, no discards remain but another hand does: compare the supplied two-play totals and rankings, not just immediate score. A setup play spends a hand to preserve a promising draw. Weigh poor-draw totals and chance_two_plays_clear as well as the average; a high average alone does not guarantee survival. The forecast assumes our best modeled next play and includes misses; it does not plan the whole round. Choose for survival rather than build preference.
instructions.best_discard: If we discard, which plan best helps us survive this round? Options are ordered by measured survival value. Each models our best next play after the draw, including misses and cards held for joker effects. Prefer better average score and downside; with one hand left, prefer the chance to clear. These are sampled scoring estimates, so account for unmodeled joker effects. Use build fit only to break close choices, never to justify a clearly worse survival outlook.
instructions.item_value: How much would taking the item in `item` (described in this question) strengthen this run? `next_boss_clear`, `survive_horizon`, `boss_margin` and `blinds_cleared_horizon` simulate the next blinds with this item and the build otherwise frozen (see `forecast`): trust them for scoring power and add what they cannot see (money, later purchases). `measured_gain`, when shown instead, is its measured effect on the scores of our recent hands, jokers included: trust it for the immediate effect and add what it cannot see (scaling over the run, money, risk, future hands). `use` says what a tarot or spectral would do for us; `worth` says what a voucher gives for the rest of the run. Favour items that fit `our_build`. Consider `engine.missing`, `upcoming_boss` and what it costs. `readiness` compares our typical hand with what the next blinds need per hand and `plan` says whether to spend on power or save. With little scoring support, prefer reliable Mult and useful temporary jokers over an xMult effect whose activation conditions are not met. `known_effect` restores missing card text. For a free pack pick, follow `pack_selection`; do not charge its pack price again.

options.blind_play: Play the {name} (need {score} chips) and earn its cash reward
options.blind_skip: Skip the {name} to gain the {tag_name}: {tag_effect}. Skipping forgoes the blind's money and shop visit.
